title: What Tunnel Network Cities Is
definition: Tunnel Network Cities: cities with freight and transit running underground.
description:
Tunnel Network Cities is cities with freight and transit running underground. It sits squarely in Future Cities & Habitats, the frontier where subway districts science becomes tube transit infrastructure.

The stakes are station blocks-scale. Societies that master tunnel hulls early will shape boring logistics practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why subway districts programs worldwide now treat Tunnel Network Cities as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Tunnel Network Cities needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

t: Real Research Today: Tunnel Network Cities
title: Real Research Today: Tunnel Network Cities
definition: Today's documented research behind Tunnel Network Cities.
description:
The road to Tunnel Network Cities is already being paved. Sidewalk Labs' Quayside (Toronto) piloted sensor-rich urban design before its 2020 cancellation. The C40 Cities network coordinates 90+ megacities on climate adaptation and emissions cuts.

The EU's 100 Climate-Neutral Cities mission funds urban decarbonization pilots. Together these programs form the subway districts foundation that Tunnel Network Cities will build on — the tube transit results, the boring logistics methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as tube transit research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: The tunnel hulls Grid
definition: The tunnel hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Tunnel Network Cities.
description:

In the Tunnel Network Cities architecture, the tunnel hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the tunnel hulls fails outright — Tunnel Network Cities stops being Tunnel Network Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works.

t: 2030 — The first tunnel hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first tunnel hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Tunnel Network Cities roadmap.
description:
The first tunnel hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its subway districts grid and tube transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the subway districts results have to replicate outside the lab, tube transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and boring logistics operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed subway districts demonstrations, tube transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting boring logistics uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Tunnel Network Cities
definition: Estimates Tunnel Network Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Tunnel Network Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a tunnel hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Tunnel Network Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Tunnel Network Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Tunnel Network Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 75293 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where subway districts monitoring, tube transit redundancy, or boring logistics maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Tunnel Network Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Tunnel Network Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Tunnel Network Cities — cities with freight and transit running underground.

Phase 1 — Prove (subway districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (tube transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (boring logistics): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (station blocks): tunnel hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and subsurface-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
